reason: The triclinic metric is well supported by peak positions (the trajectory indexes 30 reflections with about 0.008 degrees RMS error), and Z=1 is compositionally and volumetrically plausible, but exact structure recovery is not sufficiently established. No comparable Rwp is available; the selected model was ranked by a fixed-width Pearson correlation of 0.938, which still corresponds to a large unweighted whole-profile residual (about 34%) and leaves major intensity discrepancies. More importantly, both submitted P1 models are unconstrained stochastic local minima with physically implausible coordination: multiple Ta/Ti-O distances are about 1.65-1.70 angstrom, La shells are sparse/abnormal, and the trajectory explicitly found that chemically regularized coordination could not retain the diffraction fit. P1 removes extinction constraints, while higher symmetry, element ordering, and alternative chemically coherent frameworks were not systematically instantiated and compared; the two submitted models only sample two arbitrary P1 basins in the same cell. Thus the cell and perhaps an average heavy-atom intensity solution have support, but the submitted symmetry, oxygen coordinates, occupancies/order realization, and framework do not, and another scientifically motivated solution attempt is warranted.
